title: Why FBR POS Integrations Fail at Go-Live (and How to Prevent It)
metaDescription: The real reasons FBR POS integrations fail when businesses go live in Pakistan — untested invoices, wrong credentials, no offline plan — and how to avoid each.
content:
Most integrations fail for boring reasons

When an FBR POS integration breaks right after go-live, it is rarely an exotic technical fault. It is almost always something ordinary that nobody tested: credentials entered wrong, no sample invoices verified in IRIS, token refresh not configured, or no offline plan. The integration looked fine in the showroom and failed the first busy afternoon. The good news is that the same predictability that causes these failures also makes them easy to prevent.

The usual causes

  • Going live without test invoices — nobody confirmed that sample sales actually reached IRIS.
  • Misconfigured API credentials — the token or key is wrong, so every submission silently fails.
  • No token-refresh logic — sales work for an hour, then stop when the token expires.
  • No offline queue — the first connectivity drop loses invoices.
  • Untested edge cases — voids, refunds, and split bills behave differently than expected.

A go-live checklist that prevents failure

  1. Verify credentials by submitting a single test invoice and finding it in IRIS.
  2. Run five varied test sales — standard, exempt, void, refund, large amount.
  3. Confirm token refresh by testing past the one-hour mark.
  4. Simulate an outage — disconnect, make a sale, reconnect, confirm it syncs with the right timestamp.
  5. Train staff on what a verified invoice looks like.
  6. Reconcile day one — match the day's sales to IRIS before trusting the setup.

A real example

A retailer in Islamabad went live on a Friday with no testing. The credentials were correct, but token refresh was off — so after the first hour nothing reached FBR. The weekend's sales were almost entirely unreported, discovered only on Monday. Thirty minutes of go-live testing would have caught it before a single real sale.

Prevention beats repair

Treat go-live as a test event, not a switch you flip and walk away from. If your integration is already failing, the fixes are usually configuration-level — our guide to common FBR POS issues walks through token, sync, and QR problems, and the IRIS registration guide covers credential setup.

faqs.question: Why do FBR POS integrations fail right after go-live?
faqs.answer: Usually because the business went live without testing — credentials were misconfigured, no sample invoices were verified in IRIS, or the offline plan was never set up. The failures were built in on day one and only surface under real use.

faqs.question: How do I know if my integration actually works?
faqs.answer: Run test invoices before going live and confirm each appears in your IRIS dashboard. If they do not show up there, the integration is not working, regardless of what the receipt shows.

faqs.question: What is the most overlooked go-live step?
faqs.answer: Configuring and testing offline queueing. Businesses test on a good connection, go live, then lose invoices the first time the internet drops during trading.

faqs.question: Can a failed integration be fixed without starting over?
faqs.answer: Almost always. Most go-live failures are configuration issues — credentials, token refresh, tax mapping, offline settings — that are corrected without replacing the system.
